notes: PUBLISHED FOR EARLY TESTING ONLY: this circuit is unreviewed, AI-generated code. The crate's planned expert security review (sha256_var/mso_splice/onehot_cursor/digest_id_extract, plus a known ECDSA range-check gap) has not landed. Do not treat as vouched-for or production-ready; do not rely on it for real relying-party trust decisions. | Supersedes r10: independent human review flagged that ClaimDigestStepCircuit::public_values exposed an undisclosed claim's raw SHA-256 digest publicly regardless of disclosure - a real cross-presentation correlation leak. Both circuits now expose SHA256(digest || nonce) instead (nonce fresh per presentation); the step<->core binding check moved from reconstructing the real MSO z from raw digests to a direct per-slot blinded-digest comparison, which also let the previously-exposed z itself stop being public (it was also a stable per-credential value). Also enables LTO for release builds (~5% perf) and widens MAX_VAR_MESSAGE_BYTES 128->176 for a real 136-byte PID claim seen in live testing. This changes the circuit's constraint wiring and public-value shape, so r10 keys/proofs are not interchangeable with r11's.
